messages.subject: re: Correlated disturbances in model - how do we handle it in R lavaan
parts:
Sheila,

>>>
Could you explain why its necessary to do the steps under RC.mod.sim.
>>>

I am not sure what "under" means here. If you mean the model syntax
assigned to RC.mod.sim, then this is the model that I used to simulate
the data in the assignment to RC.df. If you mean the steps after the
assignment to RC.mod.sim, here is an overview of the script: (1) define
RC.mod.sim to be simulated, (2) define RC.mod.est to be estimated, (3)
simulate data as RC.df, (4) fit model as RC.fit, (5) confirm the
intended model, (6) evaluate the fit and parameter estimates. If you
have data, you do not need the steps that simulate data.

>>>
Could you clarify why do we need to introduce 0.5 in the variance of
y1 (y1~ 0.5y1 - why the need to introduce 0.5 y1) and subsequently
0.25 in the covariance between y1 and y2.
>>>

To simulate data, you need to fully specify the model, including
parameter values. I just tried to pick values that seemed sensible.
These values are used to simulate the data, but estimated when the
model is fit using RC.mod.est. You can try running the script with
different values. The important thing to note is that the model
estimates do a good job of recovering the simulated values.

I hope that clears things up. Good luck.

Keith
